title: Isaiah Chapter 15 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Isaiah chapter 15 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Isaiah Chapter 15 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Isaiah Chapter 15.

questions.question: Which cities of Moab are mentioned as being laid waste in the night?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 15:1 states that Ar of Moab and Kir of Moab are laid waste in the night.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 15, where has someone gone up to weep?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 15:2 says he is gone up to Bajith and to Dibon, the high places, to weep.

questions.question: What will happen to the hair and beard of the people of Moab according to Isaiah 15?
options: Their heads shall be bald and every beard cut off
They will grow long and unkempt
questions.correctAnswer: Their heads shall be bald and every beard cut off
questions.explanation: Isaiah 15:2 mentions that on all their heads shall be baldness, and every beard cut off.

questions.question: What will the people of Moab gird themselves with in their streets?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 15:3 states that in their streets they shall gird themselves with sackcloth.

questions.question: Where will the people of Moab howl and weep abundantly?
options: On the tops of their houses and in their streets
questions.correctAnswer: On the tops of their houses and in their streets
questions.explanation: Isaiah 15:3 says on the tops of their houses and in their streets, every one shall howl, weeping abundantly.

questions.question: True or False: The city of Heshbon will cry out and its voice shall be heard unto Jahaz.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 15:4 states that Heshbon shall cry, and Elealeh; their voice shall be heard even unto Jahaz.

questions.question: Which of these places does NOT appear in Isaiah 15 as a location where Moab shall howl or cry?
questions.explanation: Jerusalem is not mentioned in Isaiah 15; the chapter mentions Eglaim, Beerelim, and Nebo as places related to Moab's mourning.

questions.question: What animal is described as an 'heifer of three years old' to which Moab's fugitives will flee?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 15:5 says that Moab’s fugitives shall flee unto Zoar, an heifer of three years old.

questions.question: True or False: The waters of Nimrim are described as abundant and full of green grass.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 15:6 states the waters of Nimrim shall be desolate; the hay is withered away, and there is no green thing.

questions.question: What will happen to the abundance and that which Moab has laid up?
options: They shall carry it away to the brook of the willows
They will give it as offerings
questions.correctAnswer: They shall carry it away to the brook of the willows
questions.explanation: Isaiah 15:7 says the abundance they have gotten shall they carry away to the brook of the willows.

questions.question: What is said about the waters of Dimon?
options: They shall be full of blood
They shall be sweet and pure
questions.correctAnswer: They shall be full of blood
questions.explanation: Isaiah 15:9 states the waters of Dimon shall be full of blood.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 15 describes Moab raising up a cry of destruction in the way of Horonaim.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 15:5 declares that in the way of Horonaim they shall raise up a cry of destruction.

questions.question: Which place is mentioned first in Isaiah 15 as being laid waste?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 15:1 mentions Ar of Moab first as being laid waste in the night.

questions.question: Which of these is a high place mentioned in Isaiah 15?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 15:2 refers to Bajith and Dibon as the high places.

questions.question: True or False: Every beard in Moab will remain uncut according to Isaiah 15.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 15:2 says every beard shall be cut off, so the statement is false.

medium.title: Isaiah Chapter 15 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Isaiah Chapter 15 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What cities are mentioned as crying out in Isaiah 15 due to Moab's distress?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 15:4 states that 'Heshbon shall cry, and Elealeh: their voice shall be heard even unto Jahaz,' indicating these cities' mourning. This connects with the overall theme of lament in verses 1-4.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 15:5, to what place will Moab’s fugitives flee?
questions.explanation: Verse 5 says, 'his fugitives shall flee unto Zoar, an heifer of three years old,' showing Zoar as a refuge. This ties with the fleeing and weeping theme in the surrounding verses 4 and 6.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 15:6 describe about the waters of Nimrim?
options: They shall be full of fish
They shall be sweet and refreshing
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'For the waters of Nimrim shall be desolate,' emphasizing the devastation. This matches the withering of hay and grass also described in the same verse.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 15:4 illustrate the emotional state of Moab's soldiers?
options: They cry out, and their life is grievous
questions.correctAnswer: They cry out, and their life is grievous
questions.explanation: The verse says, 'therefore the armed soldiers of Moab shall cry out; his life shall be grievous unto him,' showing deep anguish among the fighters, consistent with the mourning in the chapter.

questions.question: What is the significance of the 'heifer of three years old' mentioned in Isaiah 15:5?
options: It symbolizes Zoar as a place of refuge
It refers to a sacrificial offering
It is a metaphor for the enemy’s army
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes Zoar as a place of refuge
questions.explanation: Verse 5 uses this phrase to describe Zoar, indicating a place of protection and gentleness amidst destruction, linking to the fleeing of Moab's people.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 15 teach about responding to calamity based on the example of Moab?
options: Express sorrow openly and seek refuge
Ignore the problem and hope it passes
questions.correctAnswer: Express sorrow openly and seek refuge
questions.explanation: The chapter shows Moab’s mourning (verses 2-4) and fleeing to Zoar for safety (verse 5), teaching believers to acknowledge grief and seek God’s protection.

questions.question: What does the withering of hay and failing grass in Isaiah 15:6 symbolize in a spiritual context?
options: Spiritual desolation and loss of vitality
A season of harvest and plenty
questions.correctAnswer: Spiritual desolation and loss of vitality
questions.explanation: The verse mentions 'hay is withered away, the grass faileth, there is no green thing,' which metaphorically suggests spiritual barrenness during trials, connecting to the mourning theme.

questions.question: Based on Isaiah 15:4-5, how can believers find hope in times of distress?
options: By crying out to God and seeking refuge
By relying solely on their own strength
By ignoring pain and pretending all is well
questions.correctAnswer: By crying out to God and seeking refuge
questions.explanation: The passage shows Moab crying out (verse 4) and fleeing to Zoar (verse 5), teaching that lament and seeking God’s protection are appropriate responses to hardship.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 15:7 predict will happen to the abundance Moab has gathered?
options: They shall carry it away to the brook of willows
They shall store it safely in their cities
They shall offer it as sacrifices
They shall share it generously with neighbors
questions.correctAnswer: They shall carry it away to the brook of willows
questions.explanation: Verse 7 states, 'Therefore the abundance they have gotten... shall they carry away to the brook of the willows,' implying loss and forced relocation of goods.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 15:8 describe the spread of Moab’s cry of distress?
options: It goes round about the borders of Moab
It is confined to one city
questions.correctAnswer: It goes round about the borders of Moab
questions.explanation: The verse says, 'the cry is gone round about the borders of Moab,' indicating widespread mourning consistent with the chapter's theme.

questions.question: What is the meaning of the waters of Dimon being 'full of blood' in Isaiah 15:9?
options: It symbolizes violence and judgment on Moab
It means the waters are contaminated with dirt
It is a sign of healing
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes violence and judgment on Moab
questions.explanation: Verse 9 states, 'the waters of Dimon shall be full of blood,' which metaphorically reflects the judgment and destruction coming upon Moab, supported by the mention of lions and remnant.

questions.question: True or False: According to Isaiah 15:4, the voice of Heshbon and Elealeh will not be heard beyond their own cities.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 15:4 says their voice 'shall be heard even unto Jahaz,' indicating that their cries will be heard beyond their cities.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 15:6 teaches that when the natural resources fail, it reflects a deeper spiritual or communal crisis.
questions.explanation: The verse describes the desolation of waters and withering grass, often symbolizing spiritual barrenness or judgment, which aligns with the surrounding context of Moab's suffering.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 15:5 indicates that Moab’s people will find peace and joy in Zoar without any sorrow.
questions.explanation: Verse 5 says fugitives flee to Zoar 'for by the mounting up of Luhith with weeping shall they go it up,' showing that sorrow accompanies their flight, not peace and joy.

questions.question: How does the mourning described in Isaiah 15:2-3 teach believers about humility in trials?
options: By showing the importance of openly expressing grief
By encouraging hiding emotions from others
By ignoring pain and pretending all is well
questions.correctAnswer: By showing the importance of openly expressing grief
questions.explanation: Verses 2-3 describe weeping and girding with sackcloth, demonstrating that humility includes honestly expressing sorrow before God and community.

hard.title: Isaiah Chapter 15 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Isaiah Chapter 15.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 15:7, where will the abundance and the treasures of Moab be carried away to?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 15:7 states that the abundance and what they have laid up shall be carried away to the brook of the willows, symbolizing the loss and desolation brought upon Moab.

questions.question: In Isaiah 15:8, to which locations does the cry and howling of Moab spread?
questions.explanation: The verse Isaiah 15:8 specifies that the cry and howling of Moab have gone around the borders and are heard in Eglaim and Beerelim, indicating the widespread mourning.

questions.question: What is the meaning of the Hebrew word translated as "howl" in the context of Isaiah 15:8, and what does it signify culturally?
options: "Nakah" meaning to strike; signifying a physical attack
"Ra'ah" meaning to see; signifying a vision of sorrow
"Qowl" meaning a loud cry or wailing; signifying deep mourning
"Shama" meaning to hear; signifying the spreading of news
questions.correctAnswer: "Qowl" meaning a loud cry or wailing; signifying deep mourning
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word "qowl" used in Isaiah 15:8 translates to a loud cry or wailing, which culturally indicates an expression of intense grief and mourning, appropriate for Moab's calamity.

questions.question: Isaiah 15:9 mentions the waters of Dimon being full of blood. What literary device is primarily used here?
questions.explanation: The phrase 'waters of Dimon shall be full of blood' in Isaiah 15:9 uses metaphor to symbolize the bloodshed and violence upon the land of Moab.

questions.question: What consequence is described in Isaiah 15:9 for those who escape Moab?
options: They will find refuge in Egypt
They will be ignored by neighboring nations
questions.explanation: Isaiah 15:9 foretells that more calamity will come upon Dimon, including lions attacking those who escape Moab, symbolizing relentless judgment.

questions.question: Which other biblical passage echoes the theme of desolation and mourning over Moab as depicted in Isaiah 15?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 48 also prophesies destruction and mourning over Moab, closely paralleling Isaiah 15's themes of desolation and lamentation.

questions.question: Isaiah 15:7 and Jeremiah 17:8 share a symbolic use of a "brook" or "water source." How does Isaiah's use compare to Jeremiah's?
options: Isaiah uses it as a place of loss, Jeremiah as a symbol of stability
Both use it as a symbol of destruction
Isaiah uses it as a place of refuge, Jeremiah as a place of exile
Both use it as a symbol of military conquest
questions.correctAnswer: Isaiah uses it as a place of loss, Jeremiah as a symbol of stability
questions.explanation: In Isaiah 15:7, the brook of the willows is where Moab's abundance is carried away, symbolizing loss, whereas Jeremiah 17:8 uses a similar image to symbolize hope and stability for the righteous.

questions.question: What does the reference to "lions" in Isaiah 15:9 most likely symbolize in the historical and cultural context of the ancient Near East?
options: Actual wild lions in the region
questions.explanation: In the ancient Near East, lions commonly symbolized powerful enemies or fierce attackers, so in Isaiah 15:9, lions represent the destructive forces pursuing the remnant of Moab.

questions.question: How does the motif of "waters full of blood" in Isaiah 15:9 foreshadow New Testament themes?
options: It prefigures the blood of Christ for atonement
It symbolizes the baptism of believers
It anticipates the bloodshed in Revelation's plagues
It predicts the coming of the Holy Spirit
questions.correctAnswer: It anticipates the bloodshed in Revelation's plagues
questions.explanation: The image of waters turning to blood in Isaiah 15:9 foreshadows similar apocalyptic judgments found in Revelation, where waters turn to blood as a sign of divine wrath.

questions.question: Isaiah 15:7-9 collectively illustrate a theme of devastation. Which earlier Scripture passage also uses water imagery to convey judgment?
questions.explanation: Exodus 7:17-21 describes the Nile turning to blood as a plague on Egypt, paralleling Isaiah 15:9's depiction of waters of Dimon filled with blood as judgment on Moab.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 15:8 describes the cry and howling of Moab as confined only within the city of Kir Moab.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 15:8 states the cry goes round about the borders of Moab and reaches Eglaim and Beerelim, showing the mourning spreads widely, not confined to Kir Moab.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 15:7 implies that Moab's stored wealth will not be lost but preserved within its borders.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 15:7 clearly states the abundance and what they have laid up will be carried away to the brook of the willows, indicating loss, not preservation.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 15 function as an inclusio with the references to Ar and Kir of Moab in verses 1 and 2?
options: It frames the prophecy by naming key cities at start and end
It uses Ar and Kir to symbolize the entire nation, framing the lament
It repeats the names for emphasis on military defeat
It contrasts the prosperity of Ar and Kir with Moab's ruin
questions.correctAnswer: It uses Ar and Kir to symbolize the entire nation, framing the lament
questions.explanation: The mention of Ar and Kir at the beginning (v1) and allusions later serve as an inclusio, framing the chapter and symbolizing the total devastation of Moab.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of lamentation over nations as seen in Isaiah 15's mourning over Moab?
questions.explanation: Luke 19:41-44 records Jesus weeping over Jerusalem, echoing the theme of lamentation over a nation’s impending judgment similar to Isaiah's lament over Moab.

questions.question: What is the authorial intent of Isaiah 15 in the context of the original audience in Judah?
options: To warn Judah through the example of Moab’s destruction
To encourage Judah to ally with Moab
questions.correctAnswer: To warn Judah through the example of Moab’s destruction
questions.explanation: Isaiah 15 serves as a warning to Judah by illustrating the fate of Moab as a result of divine judgment, reminding Judah of the consequences of sin and rebellion.

theological.title: Isaiah Chapter 15 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Isaiah Chapter 15 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 15:1 indicate about the fate of Moab?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 15:1 states that 'in the night Ar of Moab is laid waste,' indicating the destruction and desolation that will come upon Moab.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 15:3, what are the people of Moab doing in response to their sorrow?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 15:3 mentions that 'In their streets they shall gird themselves with sackcloth,' signifying their mourning and lamentation.

questions.question: What does the expression 'baldness' in Isaiah 15:2 symbolize?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 15:2 associates baldness and cutting off beards with mourning, indicating deep sorrow and grief over their loss.

questions.question: In Isaiah 15:5, which location do the fugitives of Moab flee to?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 15:5 describes that 'his fugitives shall flee unto Zoar,' indicating where those escaping the destruction are heading.

questions.question: What is the condition of the waters of Nimrim as stated in Isaiah 15:6?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 15:6 states, 'For the waters of Nimrim shall be desolate,' indicating a complete lack of life and sustenance.

questions.question: Which aspect of God's character is highlighted by the judgment on Moab in Isaiah 15?
questions.explanation: The judgment upon Moab reflects God's justice, as seen in the destruction and consequences faced by Moab for their actions, consistent with God's character of administering justice.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 15:9 predict will happen to the waters of Dimon?
options: They shall be full of blood
questions.correctAnswer: They shall be full of blood
questions.explanation: Isaiah 15:9 states, 'For the waters of Dimon shall be full of blood,' indicating a severe judgment and the consequences of violence and death.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 15:4 depict the emotional state of Moab's people?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 15:4 shows that 'the armed soldiers of Moab shall cry out; his life shall be grievous unto him,' indicating a state of desperation and suffering.

questions.question: What might the actions of Moab in Isaiah 15:2 suggest about the nature of humanity in times of crisis?
questions.explanation: The mourning expressed by the people of Moab in Isaiah 15:2, as they weep and show signs of grief, reflects a common human response to tragedy.

questions.question: What combined teaching do verses 5 and 6 convey about the consequences of sin?
options: Sin results in sorrow and desolation
questions.correctAnswer: Sin results in sorrow and desolation
questions.explanation: Verses 5 and 6 together illustrate that the flight of Moab's fugitives and the desolation of waters signify the severe consequences of their sins.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 15:8 suggest about the extent of Moab's suffering?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 15:8 indicates that 'the cry is gone round about the borders of Moab,' showing that their suffering is extensive and affects all surrounding areas.

questions.question: What is the significance of sackcloth mentioned in Isaiah 15:3?
questions.explanation: In Isaiah 15:3, sackcloth is mentioned as a garment worn in mourning, symbolizing grief and repentance among the people of Moab.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 15 reveal about the divine attribute of God in relation to nations?
questions.explanation: The judgment on Moab reveals God's holiness, as He cannot tolerate sin among nations, leading to divine justice being enacted upon them.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that God does not intervene in human affairs. What does Isaiah 15:1-9 actually teach?
options: God is absent from the world
questions.explanation: Isaiah 15:1-9 illustrates that God is very much involved in human affairs, specifically judging Moab for their actions and ensuring justice.

questions.question: How does the cry of Moab in Isaiah 15:4 connect to their overall fate?
questions.explanation: The crying out in Isaiah 15:4 signifies the deep despair of Moab as they face imminent destruction and suffering.
